correctness.rationale: The two-state lumped Markov chain and within-part fluctuation eigenmodes reconstruct every difference of two adjacent heat rows. Their signs yield an exact l-infinity to edge-Lipschitz norm with an attaining sign input. The strict Schur orders follow respectively from a positive second-derivative integral and a reciprocal-part identity. Strictly convex negative powers give the small-time intermediate-exponent inequality and the slowest eigenmode gives the reverse long-time inequality. The analytic implicit-function theorem applied to the divided row-norm difference establishes the local crossing expansion. All boundary cases a=1, balanced parts, theta=0 and theta=1 are included. The standard-library Poisson uniformization checker passed 4880 finite assertions; analytic proof, not those finite tests, establishes all quantified claims.

value.rationale: The norm is a natural worst-case diffusion regularization coefficient, directly equal to adjacent transition-law total variation. The theorem identifies a complete and unexpected reversal of worst bipartition geometry caused solely by choice of canonical Markov normalization, with every intermediate normalization forced to reverse order across time. Its local crossing-time formula quantifies the singular boundary between these regimes. The finite formula, strict orders, and critical temporal behavior jointly address a motivated stability gap beyond routine diagonalization.
